title: Lavandula angustifolia essential oil attenuates chronic prostatitis by inhibiting PI3K/AKT and NF-kappaB signaling pathways.
authors: Wang, Jinhui; Li, Taotao; Liu, Mei; Wang, Mengmeng; Zeng, Qi; Xu, Xinyi; Xie, Yundong; Shi, Huanxian; Zhao, Chongbo; Zou, Junbo; Shi, Yajun; Guo, Dongyan; Sun, Jing; Yang, Xiaojuan; Zhang, Xiaofei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究薰衣草精油通过PI3K/AKT和NF-kB通路缓解慢性前列腺炎，虽含分子对接与动力学模拟，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Although lavandula angustifolia essential oil (LEO) has demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties, its mechanism in alleviating chronic prostatitis (CP) remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the pharmacological basis and molecular mechanisms of LEO's effect on CP. The chemical composition of LEO was analyzed using Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS), identifying 15 active ingredients. A carrageenan-induced rat CP model was used to evaluate the impact of LEO on prostate index, inflammatory markers, and histopathological changes. The results showed that LEO significantly reduced the prostate index, inhibited inflammatory markers, and improved tissue damage. Multi-omics analysis, including transcriptome sequencing, Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), network pharmacology, and metabolomics, revealed that LEO modulates key pathways such as phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/AKT) and nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-kappaB). Molecular distillation experiments and in vitro screening identified linalool and linalyl acetate as the main anti-inflammatory components of LEO. Molecular docking (MD) and molecular dynamics simulations (MDS) confirmed strong binding affinities of these compounds to AKT1 and Nuclear Factor Kappa B subunit P65 (P65), which were further validated by Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) and Western blot (WB) analyses confirmed the inhibition of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), phosphatidylinositol 3-kinases (p-PI3K), phosphorylated protein kinase-B (p-AKT), and phosphorylated Nuclear Factor Kappa B subunit P65 (p-P65) expression. In conclusion, this study demonstrates that LEO alleviates CP through the PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB pathway, primarily mediated by linalool and linalyl acetate, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic agent for CP.
abstract_zh: 尽管薰衣草精油（LEO）已显示出抗炎特性，但其缓解慢性前列腺炎（CP）的机制仍不清楚。本研究旨在探讨LEO对CP作用的药理学基础及分子机制。采用气相色谱-质谱联用（GC-MS）分析LEO的化学成分，鉴定出15种活性成分。使用角叉菜胶诱导的大鼠CP模型评估LEO对前列腺指数、炎症标志物及组织病理学变化的影响。结果显示，LEO显著降低前列腺指数、抑制炎症标志物并改善组织损伤。多组学分析，包括转录组测序、加权基因共表达网络分析（WGCNA）、网络药理学和代谢组学，揭示LEO调节关键通路，如磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶/蛋白激酶B（PI3K/AKT）和核因子kappa-B（NF-kappaB）。分子蒸馏实验和体外筛选鉴定出芳樟醇和乙酸芳樟酯为LEO的主要抗炎成分。分子对接（MD）和分子动力学模拟（MDS）确认这些化合物与AKT1及核因子kappa-B亚基P65（P65）具有强结合亲和力，并通过表面等离子体共振（SPR）进一步验证。免疫组织化学（IHC）和蛋白质印迹（WB）分析确认抑制环氧合酶-2（COX-2）、磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（p-PI3K）、磷酸化蛋白激酶B（p-AKT）及磷酸化核因子kappa-B亚基P65（p-P65）的表达。总之，本研究证明LEO通过PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB通路缓解CP，主要由芳樟醇和乙酸芳樟酯介导，表明其作为CP治疗剂的潜力。
